## H2O: Heavy-Hitter Oracle Overview

H2O (Heavy Hitter Oracle) is a KV cache eviction policy that dynamically retains a balance of recent and H2 tokens.

### Core Concept

The approach is based on the observation that a small portion of tokens contributes most of the value when computing attention scores, and these tokens are called Heavy Hitters (H2).

### Key Findings

The emergence of H2 is natural and strongly correlates with the frequent co-occurrence of tokens in the text, and removing them results in significant performance degradation.

### Theoretical Framework

The KV cache eviction is formulated as a dynamic submodular problem with a theoretical guarantee for the novel eviction algorithm.

### Performance Improvements

The paper was published in 2023 (NeurIPS 2023) and has become an influential work in efficient LLM inference.

## Overview

FastGen is a dual-phase algorithm for crafting an adaptive KV cache. During the prompt encoding phase, model profiling is conducted to discern the behavior of various attention heads, so that the most appropriate compression strategy for each head can be chosen.

## Key Features

FastGen is a plug-and-play method that reduces the memory footprint of generative inference for Large Language Models (LLMs). With the lightweight attention profiling used to guide the construction of the adaptive KV cache, FastGen can be deployed without resource-intensive fine-tuning or re-training.

## Compression Strategy

FastGen constructs the KV cache in an adaptive manner: evicting long-range contexts on attention heads emphasizing local contexts, discarding non-special tokens on attention heads centered on special tokens, and only employing the standard KV cache for attention heads that broadly attend to all tokens.

## Performance Results

FastGen can reduce the amount of memory by 50% without sacrificing quality. In the best cases, FastGen can achieve up to 55.0% latency reduction over HF with FastGen at a generation length of 16k.

## Publication

The paper "Model Tells You What to Discard: Adaptive KV Cache Compression for LLMs" was presented at ICLR 2024.

Based on the search results, here's comprehensive information about SnapKV:

## Overview

SnapKV is an innovative and fine-tuning-free approach that efficiently minimizes KV cache size while still delivering comparable performance in real-world applications. SnapKV reduces KV cache size and computational overhead in LLMs by compressing the cache based on observed attention patterns, improving decoding speed and memory efficiency without significant performance loss.

## Key Innovation: Observation-Driven Approach

The core insight behind SnapKV involves observation of attention patterns. Each attention head in the model consistently focuses on specific prompt attention features during generation, and this robust pattern can be obtained from an 'observation' window located at the end of the prompts.

SnapKV uses a small observation window at the end of the prompt to predict token importance, aggregating attention scores from queries in this observation window.

## Compression Mechanism

SnapKV automatically compresses KV caches by selecting clustered important KV positions for each attention head. SnapKV employs a pooling layer over the observation window's attention scores to select clustered important KV positions per attention head, rather than using a flat cumulative importance score across the full sequence, making SnapKV more accurate than H2O at the same cache budget.

## Performance Results

SnapKV achieves a consistent decoding speed with a 3.6x increase in generation speed and an 8.2x enhancement in memory efficiency compared to the baseline when processing inputs of 16K tokens, while maintaining comparable performance to the baseline models across 16 long sequence datasets.

The Needle-in-a-Haystack test demonstrates SnapKV's potential to precisely manage small details on extremely long input contexts with a 380x compression ratio.

## Publication

SnapKV was published at NeurIPS 2024.

## Scissorhands: KV Cache Eviction and Token Importance

Scissorhands is a system based on the hypothesis that only pivotal tokens with substantial influence at one step will significantly influence future generations, and maintains KV cache memory usage at a fixed budget without fine-tuning the model.

### Core Concept

Scissorhands manages the KV cache by storing pivotal tokens with a higher probability. The method calculates token importance by their accumulated attention scores and keeps the "heavy hitters" in the cache.

### Performance

Scissorhands reduces inference memory usage of the KV cache by up to 5X without compromising model quality, and can be combined with 4-bit quantization to achieve up to 20X compression.

### Context in Recent Research

Scissorhands introduced importance-based eviction, assuming "cache importance stability"—that a small set of entries remains consistently important. However, more recent research has questioned this foundational assumption, with newer methods exploring alternative approaches to token importance evaluation for KV cache eviction in long-context LLM inference.

## Overview

PyramidInfer is a method that compresses the KV cache by layer-wise retaining crucial context, and saves significant memory by computing fewer keys and values without sacrificing performance.

## Key Problem Addressed

Large Language Models face challenges in GPU memory usage during inference, and to accelerate inference, computed keys and values (KV cache) are stored in the GPU memory. While existing methods study KV cache compression to reduce memory by pruning the pre-computed KV cache, they neglect the inter-layer dependency between layers and huge memory consumption in pre-computation.

## Technical Approach

The key finding is that the number of crucial keys and values that influence future generations decreases layer by layer and they can be extracted by the consistency in attention weights. Different from other methods that can only compress after the KV cache has been computed, PyramidInfer can compress the KV cache in the prefill phase.

## Performance Results

Experimental results show PyramidInfer improves 2.2x throughput compared to Accelerate with over 54% GPU memory reduction in KV cache. PyramidInfer was evaluated on various scenarios including language modeling on wikitext-v2, LLM benchmarks like MMLU and GSM8K, multi-turn conversation on MT-Bench, and long context handling on LEval.

## Publication

The research was published in Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2024.

### Overview

StreamingLLM is an efficient framework that enables LLMs trained with a finite length attention window to generalize to infinite sequence length without any fine-tuning.

### The Problem

Handling infinite-length text with LLMs presents challenges, notably storing all previous Key and Value (KV) states demands significant memory, and models might struggle to generate text beyond their training sequence length.

### The Solution: Attention Sinks

An interesting phenomenon called attention sink shows that keeping the KV of initial tokens will largely recover the performance of window attention. The emergence of attention sink is due to the strong attention scores towards initial tokens as a "sink" even if they are not semantically important.

### How It Works

StreamingLLM addresses this by retaining only the most recent tokens and attention sinks, discarding intermediate tokens, enabling the model to generate coherent text from recent tokens without a cache reset.

StreamingLLM can enable Llama-2, MPT, Falcon, and Pythia to perform stable and efficient language modeling with up to 4 million tokens and more. In streaming settings, StreamingLLM outperforms the sliding window recomputation baseline by up to 22.2x speedup.
